observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: The receiver is copied from ECX at 0x00573c02 (MOV ESI,ECX) and every field access in the body is [ESI + disp]. The two arguments are read from the caller's stack AFTER 'push ebx; push esi; push edi', at 0x00573c0a (MOV ECX,[ESP + 0x10]) and 0x00573c15 (MOV EDI,[ESP + 0x10]) respectively; with ESP lowered by 12 both resolve to [caller ESP + 4] and [caller ESP + 8]. The terminal instruction is RET 0x8 at 0x00573d69, so the callee pops two argument words.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: no register result. The single observable outcome is the byte written to receiver + 0x398, which is the boolean 'the +0xcc slot is non-null' and is refreshed on every path including both early exits.

semantic_contract: Set the editor's active rigblock, given a new part pointer and a paint-region value, and refresh everything that depends on that change. The invariants, in the order the binary establishes them: (1) The region value is latched into two consecutive dwords at +0x3b0 and +0x3b4 whenever the call is not a complete no-op, and it is latched BEFORE the change is acted on, so the region updates even when the part does not. (2) Three early exits exist, and all three still refresh the boolean at +0x398: null-and-unchanged part, unchanged part with unchanged region, and post-latch identical part. (3) When there was a previous part, the function first asks 0x004a60a0 whether the new and old parts are the same kind; if an active handle exists at +0xe4 AND they are not, it runs 0x0047e6c0 and re-runs the same comparison against the handle's resolution -- and the result of that second comparison is discarded by the compiled code. It then always calls 0x0043a830 with the literal 0. (4) A null incoming part is a deselect: bit 3 of the outgoing part's +0xdc8 flags gates 0x0043e2b0, the +0xcc slot is zeroed BEFORE the outgoing part is notified through vtable slot +0x8, and a non-null +0x498 drives a 0x005cc690 refresh. (5) A non-null incoming part is a select, and is skipped wholesale when bit 1 of its flags is set. Otherwise 0x004b09b0 installs it with the ADDRESS of the +0xcc slot as its receiver, 0x004a2060 decides whether the part is 'plain' (bits 7, 20 and 1 of +0xdc8 all clear), and only a NON-plain part with a non-null +0x498 triggers the 0x005cc690 refresh. (6) A marker is emitted as 0x004a88d0(0xbb58117e) followed by 0x0043a830(1). The gate is mode-dependent: in mMode == 1 it requires a non-null +0x3c4 and a non-zero answer from 0x005ca920; in every other mode it runs unless bits 10 AND 11 of the newly installed part's flags are BOTH set. (7) In mMode == 0 with bit 8 of the +0x3c flags set, 0x00573520 is called with the now-current part. (8) Finally, +0x398 is set to whether the +0xcc slot is non-null -- on every path, including all three early exits and both arm splits.
classification_rationale: This is the strongest body in the batch: 115 instructions and 364 bytes were read in full, every field offset and every flag-bit shift is proven by a named instruction, all three early exits and both arm splits are traced to the shared tail, and one callsite was disassembled far enough to show the deselect arm being driven with a null part and a 0xffffffff region. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because material elements remain bounded, and each is named here: (1) the eleven callees are mostly unresolved -- the vtable slot +0x8 has no concrete callee because the rigblock's table is only reachable at runtime, and 0x004b09b0, 0x0043e2b0, 0x0043a830, 0x0047e6c0, 0x005cc690 and 0x005ca920 are ports; (2) the MEANING of the +0xdc8 flag bits is unknown -- only their positions and the predicates built on them are observed, and the bit numbering is a naming convention this worker assigned, not a shipped symbol; (3) the +0x498 and +0x3c4 fields are typed 'int' by the SDK yet are used here as thiscall receivers, so their real type is bounded; (4) the tag 0xbb58117e and the marker emitter's three literals are uninterpreted hashes. The reconstructed BEHAVIOUR is complete; the bound is on identity, not on mechanics.
semantic_findings: 0x00573c00 is the editor's 'set active part' transition function. It is the only function in this batch that both mutates a pointer field and fires a virtual call on the object it drops.
The result is a single byte, not a return value: +0x398 = (the +0xcc slot is non-null), refreshed on every one of the six exits.

The +0xcc slot is cleared BEFORE the outgoing object is notified (0x00573c9f then 0x00573caa), so the drop handler observes a deselected editor. Any reimplementation that notifies first would be observably different.
The region latch at +0x3b0/+0x3b4 happens before the part change is validated, so the region tracks even when the part is unchanged.

The re-bind comparison at 0x00573c6f is dead in the compiled build: its return value in AL is never read, because 0x00573c66 already clobbered the inverted flag and nothing after 0x00573c6f reads AL before the epilogue.
The 'plain part' predicate inverts the usual expectation: 0x004a2060 returning FALSE is what causes a UI refresh, so parts that carry bits 7, 20 or 1 in +0xdc8 are the ones that dirty the palette.

The marker gate is genuinely mode-dependent, and in the non-mode-1 path the polarity is 'run unless bits 10 AND 11 are both set' -- a conjunction of two separate early exits (0x00573d1f and 0x00573d26), not a single mask test.

Bit 1 of the incoming part's flags is a hard gate: when set, the install, the predicate and the refresh are all skipped and only the tail runs. That is a 'this part type is not selectable here' path, whatever the bit is officially called.

0x005c8480's payload virtual slots and this function's slot +0x8 belong to the same observed interface family: +0x4 on the value entering a slot, +0x8 on the value leaving one. Five bodies in this batch agree on that, and none of them names it.
The whole function is void and the whole result is a memory byte, so a caller that wants to know whether the selection changed must read +0x398 itself -- which the one inspected caller does not do.
unresolved_questions: What is the type of the +0x498 and +0x3c4 fields? The SDK declares both as int/pointer mixtures; the binary passes their VALUES as thiscall receivers to 0x005cc690 and 0x005ca920, so they are objects, but which classes is unknown.
